joaquin.n: Joaquin Ortega y Joaquino was born in Cebu on 11 March 1866 to Antonio Ortega y Verzosa and Juana Joaquino, according to the Ortega Reunion 2017 family-history program. The program says he studied at the University of Santo Tomas and worked with the Compania General de Tabacos de Filipinas (Tabacalera) in Carlatan, San Fernando, in 1889. The Taft Commission appointed him Civil Governor of La Union on 15 August 1901; he became the province’s first elected governor in 1902 and served through 1904. The same family-history account records later public service as Lieutenant Governor in Abra, Bontoc and Mountain Province (1905–1914), assignments involving Lepanto and Benguet (1916–1920), and Special Agent of the Bureau of Non-Christian Tribes (1920–1926). The Provincial Government of La Union confirms his appointment and elected-governor distinction and records that he died on 31 May 1943 at age 77. With Doña Francisca Lacsamana of Bangar, he raised fourteen children. The family program also recalls that he helped move women and children to safety during the American landing at the Tabacalera port, and that he raised his nephew Jesus Ortega Floirendo as his own. These latter details are from the published family account and should be read as family-history testimony, not as independently verified operational or legal records. The family research update gives his marriage to Doña Francisca Lacsamana as 11 February 1894. The master family research summary records his full name as Joaquín Vicente Eulogio Ortega y Joaquino and gives the marriage date to Doña Francisca as 11 February 1894. His parents are Antonio Ortega y Verzosa and Juana (Ana) Joaquino; the supplied summary further identifies his paternal grandparents as Joaquín Ortega y Molina and Maria Verzosa. The master findings identify his parents as Antonio Ortega y Verzosa and Juana (Ana) Joaquino, and his paternal grandparents as Joaquín Ortega y Molina and Maria Verzosa.

francisca.n: Doña Francisca Lacsamana, known in the family as ‘Lola Paca’, was born in Bangar, La Union on 9 March 1877 and died on 3 April 1964 at age 87, according to the Ortega Reunion 2017 souvenir program. The Provincial Government of La Union identifies her as the wife of Don Joaquin J. Ortega and confirms that they raised fourteen children. The supplied FamilySearch tree screenshots show Ramona Lopez Lacsamana and Evaristo Guadalupe y Villaverde as her parents; the reunion program independently identifies her brother as Leon Lacsamana. The family program preserves stories of Joaquin travelling from San Fernando to Bangar to court her, and of their Sunday routine of attending Mass. It also describes her home, ‘Daya’, as a welcoming place where relatives arriving from Manila and other distant places could stay and spend vacations, and recalls that she encouraged family gatherings. The name Doña Francisca Lacsamana de Ortega was later given to a memorial municipal high school in Bangar; Batas Pambansa Blg. 458, approved 10 June 1983, converted it into a national high school. The courtship and household anecdotes are family recollections printed in the reunion program; dates and parentage still warrant original civil or parish record corroboration. The master family research summary reiterates Ramona Lopez Lacsamana as her mother and records the marriage to Gov. Joaquín Vicente Eulogio Ortega y Joaquino on 11 February 1894 in La Union. The master findings reiterate Ramona Lopez Lacsamana as her mother and record her marriage to Gov. Joaquín Vicente Eulogio Ortega y Joaquino on 11 February 1894.

The reunion program separately describes Daya as Francisca’s open family home for relatives visiting from Manila and other distant places; it does not provide a dated record of Leon’s individual journeys. The current family research reports a first marriage under the spelling Cayetana Munar, while the reunion program’s diagram uses Catalina Munar-Lacsamana; it is not yet established whether these forms identify the same person. Family-supplied records and indexes associate Leon with children Alfredo ‘Pidong’, Joaquin, Francisco and Eduardo, and report Paz Munar Lacsamana as a sibling of Eduardo and Pidong. These relationships remain research leads pending original civil or parish records. No reliable birth date, death date, or exact birthplace for Leon has been established. The honorific ‘Don’ is retained as family usage, not as a verified official title.

manuel.name: Manuel C. “Manoling” Ortega
manuel.role: Former Governor of La Union (2007–2016) · husband of Geraldine “Denny” · father of seven named children
manuel.n: The supplied master family summary records Manoling as born 7 August 1945 in Bauang, La Union, and as having died 2 December 2025 in San Fernando, La Union, aged 80. He served as Governor of La Union from 2007 to 2016, after earlier local and congressional public service. His wife is identified in the family records as Geraldine “Denny” Ortega; the supplied summary gives her maiden-name form as Geraldine Tanaleon Ramos. Poro Point Management Corporation’s 5 December 2025 condolence notice identifies Denny as his wife and Manuel Victor “Mannix” R. Ortega as their son. The master family summary lists seven children by name; the Provincial Government article independently confirms that the couple had seven children but does not name each one. House Resolution No. 545 is identified in the House Journal as a condolence resolution for former Representative Manuel C. Ortega; the journal does not itself enumerate the seven children. The seven names above follow the supplied master family summary. The Provincial Government of La Union has also referred to the couple’s seven children without listing all names.

The archive retains her public-facing married name “Geraldine ‘Denny’ Ortega” and records the maiden-name form as a research detail rather than assuming a specific legal name order.

branchNotes.leon: Paz Munar Lacsamana is confirmed as the daughter of Don Leon Lacsamana and Cayetana Munar. Alfredo “Pidong” is also listed in their union. Eduardo, Paz and Pidong are retained as members of Don Leon’s reported sibling / descendant grouping; the supplied evidence does not justify adding an undocumented mother or inferring full siblingship for every child.
branchNotes.antonia: The reunion biography says they had no children.
branchNotes.vicenta: Carmen later married Jose Protacio Jacinto Jr.; their four sons were Rafael, Jose III, Emiliano and Francisco.
branchNotes.joaquin-jr: The family tree records his death in infancy; no descendants. A later son, Joaquin “Titing” (branch 11), is also styled “Jr.”
branchNotes.jose: The master summary records Jose Alvaro “Pepe” Ortega as born in 1900 and died on 11 May 1942 in Capas, Tarlac, following the Bataan Death March. His marriage to Paz was on 8 September 1927 in San Fernando. Six children are indexed; the three unnamed children likely died in childhood before 1944, but that explanation remains an inference, and their names stay private.
branchNotes.luis: The first five are children of Luis and Lourdes. The reunion biography also identifies Manuel “Padaw” as Luis’s son, raised by Lola Paca.
branchNotes.ramona: Ramona “Nena” Ortega and Col. Eduardo Montilla married on 7 December 1922. Their children’s roles are recorded as Francisca Sophia “Paquita” (Barangay Kagawad), Eduardo Jose “Edward” (Ambassador), Lourdes “Penny” (Entrepreneur), and Manuel “Litong” (Attorney & Conchologist). Existing descendants remain in the individual branches.
branchNotes.juanita: The reunion family-tree diagram names Juanita; the accessible program does not provide a spouse or children.
branchNotes.pacoy: The master family summary adds public-service detail for Francisco Isabelo “Pacoy” Ortega: 24 years in Congress and service as COMELEC Commissioner. Francisco “Kiko” C. Ortega Jr. is kept separate from the older “Francisco Jr.” (pacoy-francisco) entry, which the prior archive described as having died at age 14; the two identities need primary-record reconciliation before merging.
branchNotes.manuela: The reunion biography says Manuela died at childbirth one year after the marriage; no surviving child is listed. Justo Orros Sr. then married her sister Joaquina (branch 10) — the same person.
branchNotes.joaquina: The reunion program identifies Joaquina as Justo Orros Sr.’s second wife after her sister Manuela. Your draft cites FamilySearch for Justo Jr. being their son; that could not be re-checked, and the Inquirer (2013) only calls him “a cousin of the Ortegas”.
branchNotes.titing: The master summary gives Titing’s birth date as 7 November 1916, baptism as 5 January 1917, death as 20 September 1996, and burial at Lingsat Public Cemetery. His spouse is named as Felicula Ortega in the latest summary and Felicula “Fely” Nuesa in the earlier profile; retain this as an unresolved name variant.
branchNotes.concepcion: The reunion biography says she never married and had no children; she cared for her mother and nieces and nephews.
branchNotes.mary: The reunion biography names three daughters.
branchNotes.evaristo: The master family summary says Bangar municipal records verify Fr. Evaristo Guadalupe y Villaverde, OSA, as parish priest in Bangar from 1866 to 1887. The record copy is not attached to this project.
branchNotes.alfredo-pidong: The 1944 register-page scan supports the marriage entry and records Alfredo’s parents as Leon Lacsamana and Cayetana Munar. The five children listed under Alfredo and Juanita come from the family-supplied update; no individual birth records are attached yet. The latest family update identifies Linda Lacsamana Fornoles as the sixth child of Alfredo and Dr. Juanita Valdivia Lacsamana; the five already listed children are Msgr. Alfonso Ramon, Lourdes, O’Neil, Alberto and Alfredo Jr. The update places Linda in Oxnard, California, alongside relatives Romeo and John Fornoles; their exact relationships to Linda are not specified.
branchNotes.jerry: Milagros Gandingan is identified as Jerry’s wife in family-supplied notes. Their children are listed from the same update; the youngest daughter remains unnamed as Private.
branchNotes.richard-lee: Ariane Agnes is identified as Richard Lee’s wife in family-supplied notes. Their two daughters are intentionally displayed as Private.
branchNotes.mario-lac: Mario Agustin Lacsamana is recorded as a member of a parallel Lacsamana branch. Do not attach him as a biological child of Joaquin, Francisco, Alfredo “Pidong”, or Eduardo Lacsamana without evidence.
branchNotes.antonio: The master family summary identifies Antonio Ortega y Verzosa as the son of Joaquín Ortega y Molina and Maria Verzosa, and as the father of Gov. Joaquín Vicente Eulogio Ortega y Joaquino. No earlier maternal ancestry for Juana (Ana) Joaquino is supplied.
branchNotes.manuel: The master family summary identifies all seven children of Manoling and Geraldine: Pacoy III, Jennifer Joan, Geraldine Joy, Manuel Victor “Mannix” Jr., Alfredo Pablo “Alf”, Eduardo Francisco, and Joseph Francisco. Three former entries are aliases: emmanuel-victor → mannix; manoling-child-6 → eduardo-francisco; manoling-child-7 → jeff-ortega (Joseph Francisco, earlier called Jeff).
branchNotes.paz: FamilySearch index: six children (four sons, two daughters). The 2017 Ortega Reunion biography names the three surviving children recorded with Paz at her 1944 death: Kining, Mela and Cichit. The other three are likely childhood deaths according to the supplied summary, but no death dates or identities are known; all remain private.
branchNotes.justo-jr: Parents are recorded as Joaquina Ortega Orros and Justo “Titong” Orros Sr. Siblings named by the master summary: Manuel “Lito”, Agustin, Joaquin and Rosario Orros. Spouses are listed in order as earlier wife Ligaya Israel and later wife Jocelyn Abrogar. Three sons are attached to the later wife as supplied: Jonathan Justo “Jay-Jay” A. Orros, Justo “Tito” / “Justito” Orros III, and John H. Orros.
branchNotes.extended-notable-cousins: TJ Ortega, Coleen Ortega-Garcia, Ysabel Ortega, Derrick Wilquin Orros Atijera, Maricar Icay Atijera and Cedric Sonny Panis are listed as extended notable cousins based on the master family summary. branchNotes.kining: Kining is described in the master family summary as the youngest USAFIP-NL WWII veteran and later a mayor, NTA Administrator and Presidential Consultant. His birth year is approximate (c. 1928), derived from the family summary’s age-at-1944 statement; original military and civil-service records are not attached.
branchNotes.kiko-c-ortega: This profile is listed as a Pacoy Sr / Corazon Campos descendant in the master summary. It is not merged with the previous “Francisco Jr.” record (pacoy-francisco), which has a conflicting note that the person died at age 14. Do not connect or merge until a primary source resolves the discrepancy.

familyIndex.name: Don Leon Lacsamana · La Union
familyIndex.how: Leon is reported as Francisca’s brother. The updated records connect Paz Munar Lacsamana as a daughter of Leon and Cayetana Munar. His reported children / descendants include Alfredo “Pidong”, Paz, Joaquin, Francisco and Eduardo. Linda Lacsamana Fornoles is the sixth child of Alfredo and Dr. Juanita Valdivia Lacsamana. Some relationships remain family-supplied; keep the evidence notes visible. The master family summary further identifies Ramona Lopez Lacsamana as the mother of both Leon and Doña Francisca.

familyIndex.name: Munar · Garcia
familyIndex.how: Cayetana Munar and Emilia / Emiliana Garcia are listed as Leon’s first and second wives in the supplied family research. The earlier Catalina Munar spelling remains unresolved. Paz’s six indexed children are now explained separately from the three children named in the 2017 reunion biography; the other three remain private and their early deaths are only a reported inference.

familyIndex.name: Valdris · Valdivia · Bautista
familyIndex.how: Dr. Juanita Valdivia Lacsamana’s formal maiden surname is Valdivia, supported by the family update’s cited public school / civic records and the 1944 register scan. “Valdris” is retained as an earlier clerical transcription variant. Her parents are Andres Valdivia and Marcelina Bautista. Linda Lacsamana Fornoles is the sixth child of Juanita and Alfredo “Pidong”.

familyIndex.name: Viloria · Nuval
familyIndex.how: The 2 January 1955 marriage contract names Leocadio Viloria and Prisea Nuval as Concepcion’s parents. A separate update note spells the mother’s name “Prinsea”; the scan appears to read “Prisea”.

familyIndex.name: Lomiteng · Buyao
familyIndex.how: The 8 September 1958 marriage contract names Mariano Lomiteng and Rafaela Buyao as Pacita’s parents and records the marriage to Francisco Lacsamana in San Fernando, La Union.

familyIndex.name: Argueza · Rillera

familyIndex.name: Lee · Edna Lacsamana’s descendants

familyIndex.name: Separate Leon record groups

The 16 November 1962 marriage contract identifies Macario’s parents as Leon Lacsamana and Alejandra Capalad and Felicidad’s parents as Ramon Santos and Candida Lacsamana. This is not evidence that this Leon is Don Leon of La Union.

familyIndex.name: Ancheta
familyIndex.how: Antonia Ortega married Gov. Pio Ancheta, Governor of La Union 1919–1922. They had no children.

familyIndex.name: Panis · Jacinto
familyIndex.how: Vicenta Ortega married Col. Emiliano Panis, a surgeon and lawyer. Their daughter Carmen later married Jose Protacio Jacinto Jr.; they had four sons.

familyIndex.name: Balingit · Dacanay · Alviar
familyIndex.how: Through the children of Jose Alvaro Ortega and Paz Munar Lacsamana, who married on 8 September 1927: six children are reported (four sons and two daughters). Kining, Mela and Cichit are named; three other children remain unnamed in the supplied update. Kining married Cleofe “Pet” Balingit (11 children), Mela married Santos Dacanay, and Cichit married Emily Alviar.

familyIndex.name: Rivero
familyIndex.how: Luis Ortega married Lourdes Favis Rivero; they had five children, and Luis also had a son, Manuel “Padaw”.

familyIndex.name: Montilla · Maglaya · Manguerra · Kleindienst
familyIndex.how: Ramona Ortega married Col. Eduardo Resurreccion Montilla. Their children married Froilan Benitez Maglaya (Paquita), Maria Victoria “Vicky” Manguerra (Edward) and Rolf Kleindienst (Penny).

familyIndex.name: Campos
familyIndex.how: Francisco “Pacoy” Ortega, congressman, married Corazon Campos of Bauang. Their sons Victor and Mario Eduardo carry Campos as a middle name, and several became governors of La Union.

familyIndex.name: Alviar
familyIndex.how: Vini Nola Alviar married Francisco “Pacoy” Ortega III, Governor 2016–2022; Emily Alviar married Leon “Cichit” Ortega. Whether the two Alviar families are related is not stated.

familyIndex.name: Orros
familyIndex.how: Manuela, and after her death her sister Joaquina, married Justo “Titong” Orros Sr. Justo Orros Jr., a judge and Governor of La Union 1992–2001, is placed as Joaquina’s son following your draft (the Inquirer calls him “a cousin of the Ortegas”); his son Jay-jay served on the provincial board.

familyIndex.name: Nuesa
familyIndex.how: Joaquin “Titing” Ortega, Governor 1988–1992, married Felicula “Fely” Nuesa; they had five children.

familyIndex.name: Gonong · Peralta · Cantorna
familyIndex.how: Maria Ortega married Dr. Fernandico Gonong. Their daughters are Marietta Gonong, Teresita “Tessie” Peralta and Fernandica “Dinah” Cantorna.

familyIndex.name: Ubaldo · Bolong · Argel
familyIndex.how: Evaristo Ortega married Rosa Viloria Ubaldo. Their six children include the twins Ma. Luz “Luchie” Bolong and Ma. Nila “Nile” Argel.

familyIndex.name: La Union governors · Ortega legacy

Joaquín Ortega (1901–1904), Joaquín “Titing” Ortega Jr. (1988–1992), Justo Ortega Orros Jr. (1992–2001), Victor Francisco Ortega (2001–2007), Manuel “Manoling” Ortega (2007–2016), Francisco Emmanuel “Pacoy” Ortega III (2016–2022), Raphaelle Veronica “Rafy” Ortega-David (2022–2025), and Mario Eduardo “Tot” Ortega (2025–present). familyIndex.name: Guadalupe · Villaverde · Fr. Evaristo’s family of origin

It also gives the alternate name “Muy Reverendo Padre Fray Evaristo Villaverde Guadalupe OSA.” A register-page scan and signature artwork attributed to Evaristo are preserved in the research assets; the scan has not been transcribed and the signature attribution has not been independently authenticated. The family update clarifies that Ramona Lopez Lacsamana and Evaristo did not marry; their tree link is parentage only.
